articles.title: Fiction Park: They left a city and found a home
articles.summary: A family in Kathmandu learns of an empty ancestral property from an old friend. Deciding to leave the city, they move to Fiction Park, where they start a new chapter of their lives, turning the vacant land into a home and embracing a fresh beginning away from urban life.

articles.title: Indian TV coverage of Nepal floods criticised for sensationalism
articles.summary: Indian television crews covering the recent floods in Nepal have been accused by local residents of turning their own hardships at disaster sites into sensationalist drama, focusing on spectacle rather than assisting flood victims. The criticism highlights concerns that the media's approach prioritizes viewership over humanitarian aid, potentially diverting attention and resources away from those in need.

articles.title: NEPSE edges higher as turnover jumps 26 percent
articles.summary: The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) rose by 0.66% over a four‑session week, buoyed by a 26% surge in turnover. While the modest gain suggests a tentative recovery, market analysts caution that sustained higher trading volumes are needed to confirm a lasting upturn in the market.

articles.title: Sheikh hits century as Nepal set UAE 314-run target
articles.summary: Sheikh scored a century as Nepal posted 313 for nine, setting a 314‑run target for the United Arab Emirates in the ACC Premier Cup final held in Kuala Lumpur.

articles.title: Nepal beat UAE to win Premier Cup and Qualify for Asia Cup
articles.summary: In the Premier Cup final held in Kuala Lumpur, Nepal defeated the United Arab Emirates by posting 313 for nine, bolstered by Aasif Sheikh's century. The Nepalese bowlers then restricted the UAE to 269, securing a six‑run victory. The win not only clinched the Premier Cup title for Nepal but also earned them a spot in the upcoming Asia Cup, marking a significant achievement for the nation's cricket team.

articles.title: What a telecom licence means—and what happens when it expires
articles.summary: The article explains the role of a telecom licence in Nepal, outlining the rights it grants operators such as spectrum access, service provision, and regulatory protection. It details the obligations tied to the licence, including payment of fees, compliance with service quality standards, and adherence to spectrum usage rules. Using United Telecom Limited (UTL) as a case study, the piece describes how the Nepal Telecommunications Authority (NTA) cancelled UTL’s licence after the company failed to pay required fees, and it outlines the legal and operational consequences of such a cancellation, including service disruption, asset seizure, and the need for the operator to reapply for a new licence. The article also discusses the broader impact on consumers and the telecom market.

articles.title: For some Nepali migrants, even death does not bring them home
articles.summary: The article explores the plight of Nepali migrant workers who die overseas, highlighting the heartbreaking dilemma families face when they cannot afford the cost of repatriating the bodies. Many are forced to accept foreign graves or endure prolonged waiting periods for financial assistance, underscoring the broader challenges of labor migration, inadequate support systems, and the emotional toll on families left behind.

articles.title: Saudis shut down oil pipeline as Houthis tighten grip on Red Sea shipping
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia has halted operations on its 1,200‑km oil pipeline that runs across the Arabian Peninsula, a route that previously allowed it to bypass the congested Strait of Hormuz. The shutdown comes as Houthi forces tighten their grip on Red Sea shipping lanes, threatening regional oil flow and prompting Saudi officials to reassess the pipeline’s security and strategic value.

articles.title: Explainer: Why and how EVs catch fire
articles.summary: A fatal electric vehicle fire in Bharatpur has sparked widespread concern in Nepal about the safety of EVs. The Kathmandu Post provides an explainer that addresses eleven common questions regarding why EVs catch fire, examining whether the cause lies in battery defects, charging practices, external damage, or other factors. The article aims to inform the public and clarify misconceptions, while highlighting the need for stricter safety standards and better consumer awareness as electric vehicles become more common in the country.

articles.title: Army chief Sigdel to visit China for defense and security forum
articles.summary: Nepal’s army chief, General Sigdel, is set to travel to China to attend a defense and security forum, marking the country’s return to the Beijing Xiangshan Forum after skipping last year’s event due to domestic Gen Z protests. The visit aims to deepen bilateral military cooperation, discuss regional security challenges, and re‑engage Nepal in multilateral security dialogues.

articles.title: BRICS adopts joint declaration, urges ‘maximum restraint’ in Mideast
articles.summary: The BRICS bloc has adopted a joint declaration, urging maximum restraint in the Middle East, despite the presence of both Iran and the United Arab Emirates.

articles.title: Korala border customs revenue surges as cargo diverts from closed crossings
articles.summary: Following the August floods that forced the closure of the Rasuwagadhi and Tatopani border crossings, cargo traffic has been rerouted through the Korala border. In just 15 days, customs at Korala collected about Rs1.5 billion, reflecting a sharp increase in trade volume. However, the diversion has caused transport costs to Kathmandu to soar, rising roughly 15‑fold. The surge highlights both the economic opportunity for the Korala crossing and the logistical challenges faced by traders due to the disrupted traditional routes.

articles.title: August flood death toll rises to 1386, with 5130 still missing
articles.summary: The death toll from the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods in Nepal has risen to 1,386, with 5,130 people still missing. Authorities have recovered bodies from eight affected districts, but only 104 have been identified and returned to families. The disaster has caused widespread devastation across the region, prompting emergency response efforts and raising concerns about the safety of remaining residents and the need for extensive rescue and recovery operations.

articles.title: Bhotekoshi floods push Kulekhani into continuous power generation
articles.summary: Heavy rains caused the Bhotekoshi River to flood on August 26, forcing the Kulekhani hydro‑electric plant to operate continuously to compensate for the loss of more than 400 megawatts of national power generation. The sudden shortfall has strained Nepal's electricity grid, prompting authorities to rely on Kulekhani's output while assessing damage to other facilities. The situation highlights the vulnerability of the country's power infrastructure to extreme weather events and underscores the need for resilient energy planning.

articles.title: Diversion sends traffic surging along Tribhuvan Highway
articles.summary: A blockage on the Prithvi Highway has forced thousands of vehicles onto the narrower, winding Tribhuvan Highway, causing severe congestion and turning everyday travel into a grueling experience for commuters. The sudden surge in traffic has highlighted infrastructure challenges and prompted calls for quicker road repairs and better traffic management from authorities.

articles.title: Nepal down arch-rivals UAE to secure continental spot
articles.summary: Nepal's cricket team, the Rhinos, defeated arch‑rival United Arab Emirates by 44 runs in Malaysia, securing a place in the 2027 Asia Cup to be held in Bangladesh. Aasif Sheikh starred with a brilliant unbeaten 102, leading Nepal to the continental spot alongside cricket’s established powerhouses.

articles.title: Malaysia labour row puts Nepali jobs at risk
articles.summary: Malaysia’s recent decision to restrict foreign labor recruitment to 25 designated principal agencies has sparked concerns in Nepal, where many citizens work in Malaysia’s construction and manufacturing sectors. Kathmandu officials and Nepali recruitment agencies warn that the move could jeopardize thousands of jobs and have called for high‑level talks with Malaysian authorities to seek a resolution. The dispute highlights broader issues of labor migration policies, worker rights, and bilateral cooperation between the two countries.

articles.title: Budget-friendly places for Nepali students in Daejeon
articles.summary: The article lists five neighborhoods in Daejeon, South Korea, that are suitable for Nepali students seeking affordable housing. It evaluates each area based on rent costs, proximity to university campuses and public transport, and availability of everyday amenities such as grocery stores, cafes, and internet access. The guide aims to help students balance budget constraints with convenient commutes and a comfortable living environment while studying abroad.

articles.title: Swedes vote in election that could usher far right into government
articles.summary: Swedish voters are heading to the polls to decide between a centre-left opposition that promises increased welfare spending and a right-wing coalition that advocates stricter immigration policies and a larger role for the Sweden Democrats. The outcome could see the far‑right Sweden Democrats gain influence in government for the first time, reshaping Sweden's political landscape and its approach to social policy and immigration.

articles.title: Nature doesn’t care about your climate conference speech
articles.summary: An editorial in the Kathmandu Post warns that Nepal faces a multi‑billion‑dollar adaptation gap as climate impacts intensify, while wealthy nations continue to offer only rhetorical sympathy at international climate conferences. The piece argues that talk at these meetings does not translate into the financing or concrete actions needed to protect vulnerable communities, leaving Nepal effectively drowning in the consequences of climate change. It calls for urgent, substantive support rather than empty speeches, highlighting the disparity between global pledges and on‑the‑ground realities.

articles.title: Farmers face dire consequences as floods devastate Nepal’s harvest
articles.summary: Farmers in Nepal are facing dire consequences due to floods that have devastated the country's harvest.

articles.title: ‘Bir Ganeshman’: A theatrical tribute to a freedom fighter
articles.summary: A new theatrical production titled “Bir Ganeshman” pays tribute to Nepal’s revered freedom fighter Ganeshman Singh. The play dramatizes his political activism and contributions to the nation’s struggle for democracy, offering audiences a poignant reminder of his legacy at a time when Nepal is undergoing significant political and social change. Staged by a local theatre troupe in Kathmandu, the production blends historical narrative with contemporary artistic expression, aiming to inspire reflection on the country’s past and its evolving future.

articles.title: Flood damage leaves Rasuwagadhi road facing long repairs
articles.summary: Heavy rains caused the Bhotekoshi flood to wash away roughly 40 km of the Rasuwagadhi road, a key route to the Chinese border. The Department of Roads responded by opening temporary tracks and planning the construction of Bailey bridges to restore connectivity. Officials aim to complete the repairs before the upcoming Dashain festival, emphasizing the urgency to re‑establish the cross‑border link for trade and travel.

articles.title: Trapped nine days in a dark tunnel, Nepali man tells his survival story
articles.summary: After being trapped for nine days in a dark, narrow tunnel, Nepali man Sanjay Sah was rescued on the tenth day. He survived by relying on prayer, hope, and thoughts of his family despite facing darkness, hunger, and injuries. His harrowing experience highlights the resilience and mental strength required to endure such extreme conditions.

articles.title: Two killed, four seriously injured in Rukum West jeep crash
articles.summary: A jeep traveling from Kotgaun to Khalanga in Rukum West district crashed into the Deuta Khola river within Sanibheri Rural Municipality-6. The accident resulted in two fatalities and four people sustaining serious injuries. Local authorities are investigating the cause of the crash and providing medical assistance to the injured.
